come from her. They say, too, that she will rather die than give any sign of affection.
I did never think to marry. I must not seem proud. Happy are they that hear their detractions
and can put them to mending. They say the lady is fair. Tease a truth. I
can bear them witness and virtuous. Tease so I cannot reprove it, and wise, but for
loving me. By my troth it is no addition to her wit, nor no great argument of her folly,
for I will be horribly in love with her. I may chance have some odd quirks and remnants
of wit broken on me, because I have railed so long against marriage. But doth not the
appetite alter? A man loves the meat in his youth that he cannot endure in his age.

of his humor? No, the world must be peopled. When I said I would die a bachelor, I did
not think I should live till I were married. Here comes Beatrice. By this day, she's a
fair lady. I do spy some marks of love in her.
